issues: Integrity is fine. The diff only changes how the starting points are generated: a random perimeter ring with the corners fixed, plus random interior points, all from the seeded rng. It reads no files, pastes no known coordinates and does not touch the check.

No bug makes the result meaningless. In _perim_pts, kp is at least 14, so ring points are about 0.23 apart. Each corner therefore pulls in a different nearest point and no point gets moved twice. Clipping and the SLSQP polish stay as they were.

The numbers don't support z = -4.024. There is 1 candidate run (-2.636) and 1 incumbent run (-2.6360), and they are equal at the shown precision. With n=1 on each side there is no variance estimate, so z can't be recomputed. A z of -4 would also mean a strongly better candidate, which conflicts with the provisional 'reject'.
The candidate's 2.636 is slightly above the best known 2.635. That is likely rounding (best known is about 2.6358), but check the full-precision value and that the packing is valid.
Suggest replicate runs of both candidate and incumbent before deciding. As it stands, there is no evidence of any difference.
